---
title: "Vendor & Third-Party Risk Management"
order: 103
---

## The finish line

By the end of this course you can read a SOC 2 report and an ISO 27001 certificate or Statement
of Applicability well enough to know what each one actually covers — and, just as importantly,
what it doesn't — tier a vendor's risk the way AABB's own Quality System Essentials expect, and
say precisely what a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and a vendor change notification each
legally obligate the other side to do.

This course turns the scrutiny this curriculum has spent nine courses aiming inward — at
Lakeshore's own BECS (Blood Establishment Computer Software), its own quality system, its own
eQMS (electronic quality-management system) — outward, onto the vendors underneath all of it.
Its running example is the one vendor this curriculum has already met without naming: the
device-management platform whose migration left `healthcare-security-and-privacy`'s own
Brookfield laptop incident with a permanently unresolved encryption question. This course is
where Lakeshore finally asks the question that incident raised and never got to answer: what do
we actually know about this vendor's own security posture, and what does our contract with them
actually require of them?

## Before you start

This course assumes the foundations and three earlier courses:

- [Reading a CFR citation](../../foundations/reading-a-cfr-citation/index.qmd),
  [Regulatory landscape orientation](../../foundations/regulatory-landscape-orientation/index.qmd),
  and [Risk and controls vocabulary](../../foundations/risk-and-controls-vocabulary/index.qmd).
- [Quality System Essentials](../quality-system-essentials/index.qmd), especially its
  [change control](../quality-system-essentials/index.qmd) module — this course's final module
  places a vendor's own change-notification obligations directly against that content, never
  re-teaching change control from scratch.
- [GRC Frameworks & Risk Management](../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/index.qmd), for the
  categorize/tier-by-impact vocabulary this course reuses when tiering a vendor's own risk.
- [Healthcare Security & Privacy](../healthcare-security-and-privacy/index.qmd), for the
  device-management platform vendor and its migration, the incident this course picks back up.

## The five modules

Each module is one sitting, and each has its own finish line.

1. **Supplier qualification and risk tiering.** Apply AABB's own Quality System Essential for
   supplier and customer issues to a real vendor decision: which vendors need deep qualification
   and which don't, and why that's a risk-tiering question, not a one-size-fits-all checklist.
2. **Reading a SOC 2 report.** Tell a Type I report from a Type II, name the five Trust Services
   Criteria a report can cover, and read a report's own complementary-user-entity-controls section
   and bridge letter for what they actually mean for Lakeshore's own responsibilities.
3. **Reading an ISO 27001 certificate and Statement of Applicability.** Know what a certificate
   actually certifies (a management system, not a guarantee of zero incidents), and read a
   Statement of Applicability to see which Annex A control domains a vendor actually claims and
   which it's excluded, with a stated reason.
4. **Business Associate Agreements.** Walk the actual HIPAA text requiring a BAA's contract terms
   — what it obligates a vendor to do, report, and return or destroy — using the device-management
   platform vendor as the concrete case.
5. **Vendor change notifications and your own change control.** Place a vendor's own
   change-notification and incident-reporting duties directly against Lakeshore's own change
   control process, and close this course by returning, one more time, to the still-unresolved
   Brookfield incident with the one new lens this course adds.

## A note on sources

- **AABB's own Quality System Essentials** — QSE 4, "Supplier and Customer Issues," named and
  themed only (no Standards text), the same handling this curriculum gives every AABB Standard.
- **SOC 2 (AICPA's System and Organization Controls framework)** and **ISO/IEC 27001** are both
  paid, proprietary frameworks never independently fetched or quoted in this curriculum — named
  and described in this course's own words, the same paraphrase-only handling already given to
  ISO 31000 and ISO 19011 elsewhere.
- **45 CFR 164.314(a) and 164.504(e)** — the actual HIPAA text requiring a Business Associate
  Agreement's contract terms, fetched and quoted in full, never paraphrased from memory.

Modules appear in the sidebar as they're built.
